featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

featured_reviews.name: MR. SONU KUMAR
featured_reviews.review_text:
Film City, located in Goregaon, Mumbai, is a must-visit destination for anyone passionate about Indian cinema. Spread over a vast area, it serves as the heart of Bollywood, where a large number of movies, TV shows, and advertisements are filmed. The infrastructure is impressive, with various studios, sets, and outdoor locations that offer everything from rural villages to urban landscapes. It provides a fascinating behind-the-scenes glimpse into the world of filmmaking.
One of the highlights of visiting Film City is the guided tour, which takes you through the different sets and studios where many iconic scenes from famous Bollywood films were shot. The knowledgeable guides share interesting anecdotes and stories about the film industry, enhancing the overall experience. Visitors may even catch live shooting or spot a celebrity in action!
However, Film City is primarily a working studio, so access to certain areas can be restricted depending on the ongoing shoots. The place lacks recreational amenities for tourists, and unless you're a true film enthusiast, the tour may feel a bit limited.
Despite this, Film City offers a unique opportunity to witness the magic of Bollywood firsthand. It’s especially enjoyable for fans of Indian cinema and those curious about film production. While it could benefit from more tourist-oriented facilities, its significance as a cultural and cinematic hub makes it an unforgettable experience for movie lovers visiting Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Sam Greenway
featured_reviews.review_text:
The worst tour/tourist experience in Mumbai, particularly bad if you're a foreigner paying the higher rate for the 3 hour tour. If I can prevent just one more person wasting a day here I'll be happy.
To be clear, you won't see any film sets (sets are dismantled immediately after use) but there is no imitation/example set either, so there is zero insight into Bollywood movie sets. You won't even be shown inside a studio.
You won't meet anyone famous, and you are told explicitly not to talk to any actors at all if you see any.
If you don't speak Hindi you won't get any insight into either Bollywood or any film industry as the tour and the talks are 90% Hindi. Don't believe their claim that the tour is 80% English.
Half the things listed on the tour itinerary didn't happen, ie singing in a studio, dressing up in costume etc
Overall you will learn nothing about Bollywood on this tour.
The tour starts with an 'outdoor' tour where you look at the outside of different film studios. It doesn't really matter what is being shot in there as you literally just drive past the outside of the buildings. The tour guide then drove us past a tree, a famous tree apparently(!), but its an awkward stop as there are locals sleeping underneath it.
And that's it for the outdoor tour.
Next you're taken to an indoor theme park that would make your kids cry (see photos). There is a 7D cinema experience that you can get in a shopping mall for 150rupees. Then there is a talk about.. don't know it was fully in Hindi despite the ticket office saying the tour is 80% English (it's more like 10%). Then a video about special effects that foreigners are excluded from (foreigners get a 3 minute overview in a side room - a real treat considering they pay 3 times as much).
The best bit is some kids doing some Bollywood dancing, that should have been longer than 10 minutes.
Overall really amateurish which is maybe fine if you're paying local rate (or not if you read other reviews) but infuriating if you're forced to pay the foreign tax.
